definitions.title: 3.2.2 FETCH Transition Without Indirection
applicable_context:
MS = FETCH
TS = 4
IR_INDIRECT = 0

definitions.title: 3.2.3 FETCH Transition With Indirection
applicable_context:
MS = FETCH
TS = 4
IR_INDIRECT = 1

definitions.title: 3.2.4 DEFER Completion
applicable_context:
MS = DEFER
TS = 4

definitions.title: 3.2.5 EXECUTE Completion With Valid Interrupt
applicable_context:
MS = EXECUTE
TS = 4
INTERRUPT_REQUEST_VALID = 1

definitions.title: 3.2.6 EXECUTE Completion With DMA Request
applicable_context:
MS = EXECUTE
TS = 4
INTERRUPT_REQUEST_VALID = 0
/DMA_REQ = 0
constraints: The interrupt decision has priority over DMA entry.
`/DMA_REQ` must be established before TS4.
DMA entry must be selected through the control word.
The DMA arbiter does not modify `MS_NEXT`.

definitions.title: 3.2.7 EXECUTE Completion Without Interrupt or DMA
applicable_context:
MS = EXECUTE
TS = 4
INTERRUPT_REQUEST_VALID = 0
/DMA_REQ = 1

definitions.title: 3.2.8 INTERRUPT Completion
applicable_context:
MS = INTERRUPT
TS = 4

definitions.title: 3.2.9 DMA Continuation
applicable_context:
MS = DMA
TS = 4
/DMA_REQ = 0
constraints: `/DMA_REQ` is the aggregate CPU-facing request.
The request value used by CPU control must settle before TP4.
DMA continuation must be selected through the control word.
External DMA ownership must not modify `MS_NEXT`.

definitions.title: 3.2.10 DMA Exit
applicable_context:
MS = DMA
TS = 4
/DMA_REQ = 1
constraints: The selected controller and arbiter prepare release decisions before TP4.
CPU ownership resumes in the following FETCH TS1.
CPU and DMA ownership must not overlap.

definitions.title: 3.3.2 Continued Running
applicable_context:
RUN = 1

AND

none of the following halt conditions applies at the current TP:

- a pending halt request is consumed at an instruction-completion boundary
- Single Instruction mode reaches an instruction-completion boundary
- Single Step mode reaches completion of the current major state
constraints: Preservation of the running state is explicit.
`RUN_NEXT = 1` must not be inferred from the field default.
Single Instruction mode does not halt before instruction completion.
Single Step mode does not halt before completion of the current major state.
Execution never halts in the middle of a major state.

definitions.title: 3.3.3 Start
applicable_context:
RUN = 0
FP_START = 1
the START command is accepted

definitions.title: 3.3.4 Continue
applicable_context:
RUN = 0
FP_CONTINUE = 1
the CONTINUE command is accepted
FP_START = 0

definitions.title: 3.3.6 Pending-Halt Consumption
applicable_context:
RUN = 1
HLT_REQ = 1
the current TP is an instruction-completion boundary
state_commits:
RUN     <- 0 at TP
HLT_REQ <- 0 at TP
constraints: A pending STOP or HLT request is consumed only at an instruction-completion boundary.
Consumption transitions the processor to the halted state.
Consumption clears the pending halt request at the same TP.
`RUN_NEXT` and `HLT_REQ_NEXT` are derived from the current committed `HLT_REQ` value.
A new halt request must be committed before the instruction-completion decision that consumes it.

definitions.title: 3.3.7 Single Instruction Halt
applicable_context:
RUN = 1
FP_SINGLE_INSTRUCTION = 1
the current TP completes the instruction
constraints: Single Instruction mode executes one complete instruction.
It does not modify instruction behavior.
It changes only when execution halts.
It must not halt after FETCH when DEFER or EXECUTE remains part of the current instruction.
If `HLT_REQ = 1` at instruction completion, the pending halt request is consumed and `HLT_REQ_NEXT = 0`.
If no halt request is pending, Single Instruction mode does not create one.

definitions.title: 3.3.8 Single Step Halt
applicable_context:
RUN = 1
FP_SINGLE_STEP = 1
TS = 4
constraints: Single Step mode does not initiate execution.
Single Step mode does not modify the behavior of the major state being executed.
Execution does not halt before completion of TS4.
Resumption requires START or CONTINUE.
Single Step does not create a pending halt request.
If `HLT_REQ = 1` and the Single Step boundary is not an instruction-completion boundary, `HLT_REQ_NEXT = 1`.
If `HLT_REQ = 1` and the Single Step boundary is also an instruction-completion boundary, the pending halt request is consumed and `HLT_REQ_NEXT = 0`.

definitions.title: 3.4.2 No Pending Halt
applicable_context:
HLT_REQ = 0
no STOP request is accepted
IR_OPR_HLT = 0
constraints: Preservation of the clear state is explicit.

definitions.title: 3.4.3 STOP Request Capture
applicable_context:
FP_STOP = 1
the STOP command is accepted
the current TP precedes the instruction-completion TP
constraints: The STOP request affects an instruction-completion decision only after the request has committed to `HLT_REQ`.
A request committed before the applicable instruction-completion TP is available to that decision.
A request not committed before the applicable instruction-completion TP does not affect that decision.
A request committed after that decision remains pending until the next instruction-completion boundary.
Consumption of the committed request is defined separately by [Pending-Halt Consumption](#346-pending-halt-consumption).

definitions.title: 3.4.4 HLT Instruction Request Capture
applicable_context:
MS = EXECUTE
TS = 3
IR_OPR_HLT = 1
constraints: The request committed at TP3 is available as `HLT_REQ = 1` to the subsequent EXECUTE TP4 control decision.
This definition covers only capture of the HLT request.
The subsequent run-state transition and request consumption are defined separately by [Pending-Halt Consumption](#346-pending-halt-consumption).
Request capture is independent of whether normal running, Single Instruction mode, or Single Step mode is active.

definitions.title: 3.4.5 Pending-Halt Preservation
applicable_context:
HLT_REQ = 1
the current TP is not an instruction-completion boundary
constraints: A pending halt request remains set until consumed.
The request must not be cleared during an intermediate TS or major-state boundary.
Preservation of the pending state is explicit.
A Single Step halt at a boundary that is not instruction completion does not consume the pending request.

definitions.title: 3.4.6 Pending-Halt Consumption
applicable_context:
HLT_REQ = 1
the current TP is an instruction-completion boundary
state_commits:
RUN     <- 0 at TP
HLT_REQ <- 0 at TP
constraints: The halt request is cleared only when consumed.
Consumption and transition to the halted state commit at the same TP.
Consumption applies regardless of whether another run-state halt condition also applies at that boundary.
Single Instruction completion and EXECUTE Single Step completion do not prevent consumption of an existing pending halt request.
A `HLT_REQ_NEXT = 1` value committed at the current TP is not available as `HLT_REQ = 1` for another decision at that same TP.

definitions.title: 4.2 Program-Counter Address Context
applicable_context:
the CPU owns the memory interface
the current memory operation uses PC as its address
constraints: This case applies to the documented instruction-fetch memory access.
`AB_SRC` defines the address source independently from `/RD`, `/WR`, `MDB_SRC`, and `MFB_SRC`.

definitions.title: 4.3 Memory-Address Register Context
applicable_context:
the CPU owns the memory interface
the current memory operation uses MA as its address
constraints: This case applies only to documented memory operations for which `MA` drives `AB`.
`AB_SRC` defines the address source independently from `/RD`, `/WR`, `MDB_SRC`, and `MFB_SRC`.

definitions.title: 4.5.1 Instruction Fetch
applicable_context:
MS = FETCH
the CPU performs the instruction-fetch memory access

definitions.title: 4.5.2 Direct MRI Access
applicable_context:
MS = EXECUTE
IR_IS_MRI = 1
IR_INDIRECT = 0
the current instruction performs a memory access
constraints: Direct MRI access never uses `DF`.
The zero-page or current-page selection determines the 12-bit address within the field; it does not change the field source.
`MFB_SRC` remains `IF` for both zero-page and current-page direct addressing.

definitions.title: 4.5.3 Indirect Pointer Read
applicable_context:
MS = DEFER
IR_IS_MRI = 1
IR_INDIRECT = 1
the CPU reads the indirect pointer
constraints: The indirect bit does not cause the pointer location itself to use `DF`.
The zero-page or current-page selection determines the pointer address within `IF`.

definitions.title: 4.5.4 Indirect Autoindex Writeback
applicable_context:
MS = DEFER
IR_IS_MRI = 1
IR_INDIRECT = 1
EAI = 1
the incremented pointer is written back to memory
constraints: Pointer read and autoindex writeback use the same field.
Autoindex processing does not change the pointer-location field from `IF` to `DF`.

definitions.title: 4.5.5 Final Indirect MRI Access
applicable_context:
MS = EXECUTE
IR_IS_MRI = 1
IR_INDIRECT = 1
the current instruction performs a memory access
constraints: `DF` applies only to the final memory access after indirect address resolution.
The indirect pointer read and any autoindex writeback remain in `IF`.
The resolved 12-bit address is supplied separately from the field selection.
`MFB_SRC = DF` does not alter the resolved address portion.

definitions.title: 4.5.6 Interrupt Entry
applicable_context:
MS = INTERRUPT
the return address is written to memory location 0000

definitions.title: 4.5.7 Console Examine
applicable_context:
RUN = 0
an EXAM command is accepted

definitions.title: 4.5.8 Console Deposit
applicable_context:
RUN = 0
a DEPOSIT command is accepted

definitions.title: 4.5.9 DMA Ownership
applicable_context:
MS = DMA
/DMA_GRANT is asserted

definitions.title: 5.1 Data Field From Instruction
applicable_context:
IR_WRITES_DF = 1
IR_DF_TO_DF is selected
constraints: `DF_VAL` is required when `DF_LOAD = 1` and `DF_SRC = Control`.
`IR_DF_TO_DF` binds the control input `IR_DF` directly to the control output `DF_VAL`.
No transformation is applied.

definitions.title: 5.2 Deferred Instruction Field From Instruction
applicable_context:
IR_WRITES_IF = 1
IR_IF_TO_DIF is selected
constraints: `DIF_VAL` is required when `DIF_LOAD = 1` and `DIF_SRC = Control`.
`IR_IF_TO_DIF` binds the control input `IR_IF` directly to the control output `DIF_VAL`.
`DIF_CLEAR` uses the same `DIF_SRC = Control` path but assigns `DIF_VAL = 0`.
`DIF_SRC` does not distinguish between `IR_IF` and zero; the selected control case determines `DIF_VAL`.
`IR_IF_TO_DIF` and `DIF_CLEAR` must not be selected concurrently.
No dedicated `DIF_SRC = IR` encoding or direct IR-to-DIF datapath is used.
No transformation is applied.

definitions.title: 5.3 Deferred Instruction Field Clear Value
applicable_context: DIF_CLEAR is selected
constraints: `DIF_VAL` is required because `DIF_LOAD = 1` and `DIF_SRC = Control`.
`DIF_CLEAR` and `IR_IF_TO_DIF` must not be selected concurrently.

definitions.title: 5.5.1 Read Request Acceptance
applicable_context: IO_READ_REQ is accepted
constraints: `IO_READ_REQ` and `IO_WRITE_REQ` must not both be accepted for the same request.
The accepted request must have a transfer phase and commit TP within the current external-IOT EXECUTE major state.

definitions.title: 5.5.2 Write Request Acceptance
applicable_context: IO_WRITE_REQ is accepted
constraints: `IO_READ_REQ` and `IO_WRITE_REQ` must not both be accepted for the same request.
The accepted request must have a transfer phase and commit TP within the current external-IOT EXECUTE major state.

definitions.title: 5.5.3 Completed Transfer Clear
applicable_context:
a pending transfer completes
no replacement request is accepted at the same TP
constraints: A newly accepted request does not affect the transfer committing at the same TP.
This case applies only when no replacement request is accepted.

definitions.title: 5.5.4 Completion With Read Replacement
applicable_context:
a pending transfer completes
IO_READ_REQ is accepted at the same TP
constraints: The newly accepted read request replaces the completed transfer.
The new request does not affect the transfer committing at the current TP.
The replacement request must have a transfer phase and commit TP within the current external-IOT EXECUTE major state.

definitions.title: 5.5.5 Completion With Write Replacement
applicable_context:
a pending transfer completes
IO_WRITE_REQ is accepted at the same TP
constraints: The newly accepted write request replaces the completed transfer.
The new request does not affect the transfer committing at the current TP.
The replacement request must have a transfer phase and commit TP within the current external-IOT EXECUTE major state.

definitions.title: 4.2 CPU Memory Read
applicable_context:
a CPU-owned memory-read operation is active
MEM_READ_TO_MB is selected
constraints: `/RD` and `/WR` must not both be asserted.
The CPU must not drive `MDB` during a memory read.
Memory must be the sole `MDB` producer.
The selected address and field must remain valid for the memory-read interval.
The read strobe does not itself select `AB_SRC`, `MFB_SRC`, or `MDB_SRC`.
The `/RD` & `/WR` assignments remain part of the micro-operation mappings rather than a separate direct-control assignment.
drive_states:
CPU AB driver  = driven according to AB_SRC
CPU MFB driver = driven according to MFB_SRC
CPU /RD driver = DRIVE_LOW
CPU /WR driver = DRIVE_HIGH
CPU MDB driver = HIGH_Z

definitions.title: 4.3 CPU Memory Write From MB
applicable_context:
a CPU-owned memory-write operation is active
MEM_WRITE_FROM_MB is selected
constraints: `/RD` and `/WR` must not both be asserted.
The CPU must be the sole `MDB` producer.
Memory must not drive `MDB`.
The selected address, field, and write data must remain valid for the memory-write interval.
The `/RD` & `/WR` assignments remain part of the micro-operation mappings rather than a separate direct-control assignment.
drive_states:
CPU AB driver  = driven according to AB_SRC
CPU MFB driver = driven according to MFB_SRC
CPU /RD driver = DRIVE_HIGH
CPU /WR driver = DRIVE_LOW
CPU MDB driver = driven from MB

definitions.title: 4.4 CPU Memory Write From Front Panel
applicable_context:
a CPU-owned console DEPOSIT operation is active
MEM_WRITE_FROM_FP_SR is selected
constraints: `/RD` and `/WR` must not both be asserted.
The CPU must be the sole `MDB` producer.
Memory must not drive `MDB`.
The selected address, field, and front-panel value must remain valid for the memory-write interval.
The `/RD` & `/WR` assignments remain part of the micro-operation mappings rather than a separate direct-control assignment.
drive_states:
CPU AB driver  = driven according to AB_SRC
CPU MFB driver = driven according to MFB_SRC
CPU /RD driver = DRIVE_HIGH
CPU /WR driver = DRIVE_LOW
CPU MDB driver = driven from FP_SR

definitions.title: 4.5 Inactive CPU Memory Interface
applicable_context:
the CPU owns the memory interface
no CPU memory operation is active
constraints: Deasserting `/RD` and `/WR` does not transfer memory ownership.
CPU ownership remains distinct from whether a memory cycle is active.
An inactive strobe must not be treated as `HIGH_Z` unless the interface documentation explicitly requires driver release.
Select-field defaults do not imply a memory operation.
drive_states:
CPU /RD driver = DRIVE_HIGH
CPU /WR driver = DRIVE_HIGH

definitions.title: 5.2 DMA Major State
applicable_context: MS = DMA
constraints: `/DMA_GRANT` remains asserted throughout `MS = DMA`.
CPU control must not drive `MFB`, `AB`, `MDB`, `/RD`, or `/WR`.
`AB_SRC`, `MFB_SRC`, and `MDB_SRC` may contain valid encoded values in the control word, but those values do not authorize CPU drivers during DMA ownership.
CPU-generated `/RD` and `/WR` requests remain inactive because the CPU drivers are released.
CPU and DMA ownership must not overlap.
The CPU must not select an individual DMA controller.
An external controller must not drive a DMA-owned interface unless it has a matching valid `DMA_GRANT_ID`.
drive_states:
CPU MFB driver = HIGH_Z
CPU AB driver  = HIGH_Z
CPU MDB driver = HIGH_Z
CPU /RD driver = HIGH_Z
CPU /WR driver = HIGH_Z

definitions.title: 5.3 Non-DMA Major States
applicable_context: MS != DMA
constraints: `/DMA_GRANT` must not be asserted during normal instruction execution.
External DMA controllers must not drive DMA-owned interfaces.
`DMA_GRANT_ID` does not authorize ownership while `/DMA_GRANT` is deasserted.
Pending `/DMA_REQ[n]` inputs do not themselves transfer ownership.
Aggregate `/DMA_REQ` does not itself transfer ownership.

definitions.title: 5.4 DMA Read Ownership
applicable_context:
MS = DMA
/DMA_GRANT = 0
a controller has a matching valid DMA_GRANT_ID
the selected DMA transfer is a memory read
constraints: Memory is the sole `MDB` producer.
The selected controller must not drive `MDB`.
The controller captures `MDB` at TP2.
No CPU control assignment may replace the controller-supplied address, field, or direction.
drive_states:
CPU MFB driver = HIGH_Z
CPU AB driver  = HIGH_Z
CPU MDB driver = HIGH_Z
CPU /RD driver = HIGH_Z
CPU /WR driver = HIGH_Z
external_ownership:
selected controller drives MFB
selected controller drives AB
selected controller asserts /RD
selected controller deasserts /WR
memory drives MDB

definitions.title: 5.5 DMA Write Ownership
applicable_context:
MS = DMA
/DMA_GRANT = 0
a controller has a matching valid DMA_GRANT_ID
the selected DMA transfer is a memory write
constraints: The selected controller is the sole `MDB` producer.
Memory must not drive `MDB`.
Memory captures `MDB` at TP2.
No CPU control assignment may replace the controller-supplied address, field, data, or direction.
drive_states:
CPU MFB driver = HIGH_Z
CPU AB driver  = HIGH_Z
CPU MDB driver = HIGH_Z
CPU /RD driver = HIGH_Z
CPU /WR driver = HIGH_Z
external_ownership:
selected controller drives MFB
selected controller drives AB
selected controller asserts /WR
selected controller deasserts /RD
selected controller drives MDB

definitions.title: 6.1 Inactive System Data Bus
applicable_context: no CPU DB write is active
constraints: The CPU must not drive `DB` during a DB read.
The CPU must not drive `DB` merely because an external IOT is active.
A selected external controller may drive `DB` only during its documented read-transfer interval.
At most one participant may drive `DB`.

definitions.title: 6.2 CPU DB Write
applicable_context:
DB_WRITE_FROM_AC is selected
/DB_WRITE is asserted
constraints: `/DB_READ` and `/DB_WRITE` must not both be asserted.
The CPU is the sole `DB` driver.
External controllers must not drive `DB`.
`/DB_WRITE` must be paired with `DB_WRITE_FROM_AC`.
The `/DB_WRITE` assignment and AC-to-DB datapath selection remain owned by the `DB_WRITE_FROM_AC` micro-operation mapping rather than a separate direct-control result.
drive_states: CPU DB driver = driven from AC

definitions.title: 6.3 CPU DB Read
applicable_context:
DB_READ_TO_AC is selected
/DB_READ is asserted
constraints: `/DB_READ` and `/DB_WRITE` must not both be asserted.
`/DB_READ` must be paired with `DB_READ_TO_AC`.
The CPU must not drive `DB`.
At most one selected external controller may drive `DB`.
The `/DB_READ` assignment and DB-to-AC datapath selection remain owned by the `DB_READ_TO_AC` micro-operation mapping rather than a separate direct-control result.
external_ownership: the selected controller may drive DB

definitions.title: 7.2 External-Device IOT
applicable_context:
MS = EXECUTE
the current instruction is an external-device IOT
constraints: `IOA` and `IOP` remain derived outputs rather than direct-control assignments.
Only the address-matched controller may respond.
Controller response inputs are valid only while `IOT_ACTIVE = 1`.
`IOT_ACTIVE` does not itself determine whether a read, write, skip, clear-AC, or wait response is accepted.
DB ownership remains governed by `/DB_READ`, `/DB_WRITE`, and the accepted transfer state.

definitions.title: 7.3 Non-External-IOT Control Cases
applicable_context: the current control case is not external-device IOT execution
constraints: Processor IOT execution must not qualify external controllers unless explicitly documented as an external-device IOT.
An `IOA` value alone does not make a controller response valid.
External response inputs must not affect control while `IOT_ACTIVE = 0`.

definitions.title: 8.2 CAF Initialization
applicable_context:
MS = EXECUTE
the current instruction is CAF
the current timing state is the documented CAF initialization timing state
constraints: `/INITIALIZE` is asserted for the documented one-TSTEP interval.
`/INITIALIZE` overrides normal controller activity.
Controller initialization behavior remains defined by each controller contract.
Software is responsible for satisfying documented device-idle and safety requirements before executing CAF.
`/INITIALIZE` must not be inferred from the CAF micro-operation list alone.

definitions.title: 8.3 Front-Panel Clear Initialization
applicable_context:
RUN = 0
FP_CLEAR = 1
the CLEAR command is accepted
constraints: `/INITIALIZE` is asserted for the documented one-TSTEP interval.
The associated CPU-state changes remain represented by their selected micro-operations and sequencing results.
`/INITIALIZE` does not replace those internal state assignments.
Controller initialization behavior remains defined by each controller contract.

definitions.title: 8.4 Inactive Initialization Output
applicable_context: neither CAF initialization nor accepted front-panel CLEAR applies
constraints: `/INITIALIZE` must not remain asserted beyond its documented one-TSTEP interval.
